title: Amazon E-Commerce: Complete Architecture
description: Design a scalable Amazon-style e-commerce platform with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a scalable Amazon-style e-commerce marketplace. The system must support browsing a massive product catalog with faceted search, managing a shopping cart, processing checkout and orders, tracking inventory across warehouses, generating personalized recommendations, and handling returns and refunds. Sellers must be able to list products, manage inventory, and fulfill orders. The platform must survive Black Friday-level traffic spikes while maintaining accurate stock levels.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Product catalog with categories, brands, attributes, and faceted search/filtering
Shopping cart with add/remove/update quantity and persistent cross-device carts
Checkout flow with shipping address, billing, payment method selection, and order review
Order placement with inventory reservation, payment capture, and order confirmation
Inventory management with real-time stock tracking across multiple warehouses
Order tracking with shipment status, carrier integration, and delivery estimates
Personalized product recommendations based on browsing and purchase history
Seller dashboard for product listing, inventory updates, and order fulfillment
Return and refund processing with restocking logic
Wishlist and save-for-later functionality

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Product search must return results in under 200ms even with 100M+ products
Cart operations must be strongly consistent to prevent overselling
Checkout must handle 10x traffic spikes on Black Friday and Prime Day
Inventory counts must be accurate to prevent overselling across warehouses
Recommendation engine must update user profiles within 15 minutes of activity
99.9% availability for checkout and order placement flows
Product images must be optimized and served via CDN for fast page loads

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application where product catalog, cart, orders, payments, and inventory share a single deployment and database. This validates the e-commerce domain model and transactional workflows before introducing distributed complexity.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API or MVC Controllers
  - Entity Framework Core for data access
  - Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
  - Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for product images
  - Azure Monitor or AWS CloudWatch for logging
  - Single database with tables for Products, Categories, Cart, Orders, Payments, Inventory

data.text: As traffic grows, split the monolith into independently scalable microservices. The Catalog and Cart services are read-heavy and can scale horizontally. The Order and Inventory services require strong consistency. The Recommendation service uses offline batch processing.

items: Catalog Service: Indexes products with attributes, categories, and brands. Exposes faceted search APIs and product detail endpoints. Uses Elasticsearch for full-text search and filtering.
Cart Service: Manages per-user shopping carts with add/remove/update operations. Persists carts in Redis for fast reads and writes. Publishes CartUpdated events.

Order Service: Orchestrates checkout, creates order records, manages order states (pending/shipped/delivered), and handles returns/refunds. Uses the Saga pattern for distributed transactions with Payment and Inventory.
Payment Service: Processes charges via Stripe or Braintree, handles refunds, and stores transaction history. Webhooks confirm payment success or failure asynchronously.

Inventory Service: Tracks stock across warehouses and fulfillment centers. Reserves inventory during checkout and releases it on cancellation or timeout. Uses database transactions for atomic stock updates.
Recommendation Service: Generates personalized product suggestions using collaborative filtering. Runs offline batch jobs to compute recommendations and stores them in Redis for fast lookup.
User Service: Manages customer profiles, addresses, authentication, and order history. Acts as the source of truth for user identity across services.

data.title: React App Structure
data.code:
src/
  features/
    amazon-ecommerce/
      product-list/      # Product grid with infinite scroll and faceted filters
      product-detail/    # Image gallery, specs, reviews, add-to-cart
      cart/              # Cart drawer, quantity controls, remove items
      checkout/          # Multi-step checkout: address, shipping, payment
      order-confirmation/# Order success page with tracking
      order-history/     # Past orders list with reorder and return actions
      search/            # Search bar with autocomplete and suggestions
      seller/            # Seller dashboard for product and order management
      api/               # API clients per service
      components/        # Shared UI components
      hooks/             # Custom hooks
      store/             # Zustand/Jotai state
      types/             # TypeScript interfaces
  shared/
    ui/                 # Design system
    lib/                 # Utilities
    hooks/               # Global hooks

Key Patterns:
  - Infinite scroll with Intersection Observer for product lists
  - Debounced search input with autocomplete dropdown
  - Optimistic cart updates with server reconciliation
  - Image lazy-loading and srcset for responsive product photos
  - React Query for caching catalog results and stale-while-revalidate
  - WebSocket for real-time order status updates

cards.title: Compute
cards.description: Host catalog, cart, and order API containers

cards.title: API Gateway
cards.description: Route search, cart, checkout, and seller requests
pros: Rate limiting to protect checkout from abuse
cons: Extra hop adds latency to checkout flow

cards.title: Cache
cards.description: Cache product details, cart sessions, and recommendation lists
cons: Cache invalidation complexity for dynamic pricing

cards.title: Database
cards.description: Primary store for orders, inventory, and user data
pros: Strong ACID guarantees for orders and payments
Read replicas to offload catalog browsing traffic
cons: Reserved instances needed for predictable costs

cards.title: Storage
cards.description: Store product images, seller documents, and media
pros: Cheap, durable storage for millions of product photos
CDN integration for fast page loads globally
cons: Cache invalidation for updated product images

cards.title: Messaging
cards.description: Async events for order lifecycle and inventory sync
pros: Decouples checkout from payment and fulfillment
Buffers order spikes during sales events

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: E-commerce systems require strong consistency for inventory and orders, but can tolerate eventual consistency for recommendations and reviews
Inventory reservation with TTL-based auto-release prevents overselling during abandoned checkouts
The Saga pattern manages distributed transactions across Order, Payment, and Inventory services
Catalog search is the primary scalability bottleneck—invest in Elasticsearch or Azure Cognitive Search early
Start with a monolith on Azure SQL or AWS RDS, then extract Catalog, Cart, and Order as the first microservices
data.takeaway: Amazon E-commerce is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
